Definition: neuter of a presumed derivative of the alternate of G2192 as adverb; nigh, i.e. nearly:--almost.
BiblicalUsage: Schedon is almost, nearly, and Luke uses it to measure the spread of the gospel: the next sabbath day came almost the whole city together to hear the word of God, and Paul had persuaded almost throughout all Asia that they be no gods which are made with hands.
TheologicalSignificance: What strikes me is the scale of it — almost a whole city, almost a whole province — turned by one man's preaching of the word.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
